sampling_model.design: Two-wave prospective outcome acquisition with an independent fully labelled pilot of size \(m_n\) satisfying \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), followed by a pilot-measurable deterministic-rate main-wave design \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\).
sampling_model.units: Independent main-wave records \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) have observed law \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q}\), where \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) otherwise, with fixed finite stratum space \([K]\), binary randomized treatment, and a known fixed finite outcome support \(\mathcal Y\) of size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Known propensities \(e_{ax}\) satisfy conditional randomization, and the frozen policy menu \(\pi\) maps strata to binary treatments.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment propensities are strictly positive and annotation rates satisfy \(r_{ax}\ge\rho>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The arbitrarily slowly diverging, vanishing-share pilot estimates the finitely many cell means and variances; the main wave uses the joint AIPW contrast estimator \(\widetilde\theta_n\).
sampling_model.localization: Conditional outcome arrays are \(q_n(h,v)=q^0+s(h,v)/\sqrt n\), where \(\delta_q=\min_{a,x,\ell}(q^0_{ax\ell}-\eta)>0\) ensures that every bounded positive or negative tilt lies in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). The corresponding p-indexed causal laws are \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\), with \(h\in\mathcal H\) and an iteratively expanding nuisance radius for \(v\). Conditional main-wave likelihoods are formed from \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)}\) given \(\mathscr P_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Reduces regular treatment choice with a scalar welfare contrast to a Gaussian limit experiment and transfers asymptotically minimax rules.
Establishes asymptotic minimax-regret optimality for many treatments and discusses computational-game solutions.
Derives a near-optimal two-thirds allocation for separable subgroup-specific Gaussian treatment decisions.
Derives a two-batch annotation design and AIPW estimator attaining the optimal scalar ATE asymptotic variance.
Optimizes scalar semiparametric efficiency and componentwise maximin efficiency for a fixed-dimensional parameter in two-phase studies.
Proves a semiparametrically efficient AIPW central limit theorem under adaptive treatment probabilities.
Matches exact minimax and Bayes simple-regret constants over all adaptive experiments for independent finite arms.
Obtains asymptotically Bayes-optimal two-wave design for smooth constrained policy choice under a unique, strongly concave local optimum.
Derives efficient robust estimators of smooth causal functionals under randomized double sampling.
Derives minimax-regret choice between two treatments when missing outcomes are unrestricted and treatment response is partially identified.
Solves minimax-regret treatment choice with incomplete data for finitely many treatments and shows that the two-treatment randomization pattern need not extend to three or more treatments.
Characterizes exact finite-sample minimax-regret rules for two-treatment choice with a fixed positive fraction of missing outcomes.

body.tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel covers every known fixed finite outcome support of size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes; it derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over the saturated outcome model and every contrast-preserving nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and constructs a measurable nested-cell selector, joint AIPW estimator, and refined Gaussian rule attaining that value at tied, flat, disconnected, or dyadic-boundary design optima. The fully labelled pilot may diverge arbitrarily slowly provided its share vanishes: \(m_n\to\infty\) gives finite-cell moment consistency and \(m_n/n\to0\) makes its local information negligible. The selector's spatial convergence rate remains schedule- and law-specific through the positive prefix gaps. A generic continuous-objective witness shows only that continuity plus uniform objective approximation cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it is not a model-specific impossibility theorem for the Gaussian-risk family. A rational three-policy, three-support-point witness establishes that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of the pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal annotation methods optimize scalar estimation variance, multidimensional two-phase methods optimize componentwise efficiency, and smooth policy-design theory assumes a unique curved optimum. Missing-outcome minimax-regret results instead treat exogenous incompleteness and treatment choice under partial identification; they do not choose randomized prospective annotation rates for point-identified overlapping policy loadings. None of these results combines a pilot-conditioned full-nuisance LAN transfer, correlated finite-menu regret design, nonunique deterministic selection, certified computation, and attainment with an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot whose sample share vanishes.
project_justification.niche: The niche is prospective validation of a fixed overlapping causal-policy menu when investigators control scarce randomized follow-up, the operational objective is welfare loss from the final policy choice, and only a slowly diverging fully labelled pilot can be reserved before the main wave.
project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche for known fixed finite supports of every size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes, with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, and a measurable tie-stable implementation requiring only \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\). Its joint AIPW and Gaussian-rule construction attains the minimax value, while its spatial selector rate is stated honestly as schedule- and law-specific through the certified prefix-separation profile.

body.related_work: Hirano and Porter (2009) inform the scalar fixed-experiment Gaussian decision bridge, while Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) inform finite-action Gaussian games; none observes overlapping policy loadings through selectively annotated treatment--stratum cells. The general theory here applies to a known fixed finite support of every size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes. Higbee (2026) proves two-wave Bayes design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum. Theorem 4 gives the theorem-level contrast required here: its rational \(L=3\) finite-menu specialization has a three-way tie in every local decision neighborhood and fourteen contrast-preserving selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, so Higbee's uniqueness and curvature conditions do not cover that experiment. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) supply the closest scalar annotation workflow, and the Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, supplies the nearest componentwise semiparametric two-phase criterion. Levis et al. (2024) inform observed-data influence projection, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) inform stabilized AIPW limits, and Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) identify the nonregularity of nonunique optimal decisions. Those works do not establish the present coupling of a tie-stable multivariate regret design and a discontinuous finite-policy rule under only an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot and a vanishing pilot share; the resulting spatial rate is deliberately schedule- and law-specific. Manski (2007) studies minimax-regret treatment choice when outcomes are missing for uncontrolled reasons and the response law is partially identified. Stoye (2007) extends incomplete-data choice to many treatments, and his finite-sample missing-outcome analysis studies a fixed exogenous missing fraction. Those decision problems are important antecedents but differ from prospective randomized annotation, known propensities, point-identified policy contrasts, and optimization of the acquisition design itself. Hu et al. (2024) inform regret-sensitive allocation in separable subgroup decisions. The auxiliary functional \(G_\omega\) is introduced internally only as the geometric probe in the constructive \(L=3\) witness. Codi et al. (2025) provide the stacked rule-comparison consumer, and Kim et al. (2025) motivate independent validation of the azithromycin rules. Continuous-outcome extensions remain outside the fixed-support formulation.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The nested-cell implementation is measurable and stabilizes every fixed prefix, including separated ties, flat or disconnected minimizing sets, and dyadic-boundary minima. The resulting deterministic spatial rate \(a_n(L)\) is schedule- and law-specific because it depends on both the pilot approximation envelope and the positive prefix-separation profile of the particular objective. The displayed pair \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\), both uniformly approximated by \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\), proves that continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control alone supplies no spatial recovery modulus over the generic class of continuous objectives. It does not prove that no law-uniform rate exists on the narrower Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\); such a model-specific impossibility would require a separate embedding or identification-modulus argument.
body.honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose fully labelled pilot sizes satisfy \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), and whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design; no polynomial pilot-growth condition is imposed. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, bounded pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has size \(L\ge2\) and uniformly positive cell probabilities, so binary outcomes are included; continuously supported outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, while the measurable selector has a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate determined by its pilot envelope and certified prefix gaps. The generic continuous-objective counterexample rules out a recovery modulus based only on continuity and uniform objective error; it does not establish a model-specific rate impossibility for the Gaussian-risk family. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the geometric probe in the rational \(L=3\) witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.
